evidence: The claim depends on sqlglot 30.31.0 (requirements.txt:103) parser and Expression.walk behavior. The item has no dependency_sources, and a Glob of the head view for sqlglot/parser.py and sqlglot/expressions* found nothing, so the library source was not available. The repo code at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:629-645 does check isinstance(sub, exp.Lock) in stmt.walk(), but whether every lock form (including those on a Union, in CTEs, derived tables and IN subqueries) parses to exp.Lock and is visited by walk() could not be read. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.31.0 source, or running parse_one with read='mysql' on those forms (not run).

The code at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:643-645 uses `sub.args.get("update")` to choose between 'FOR UPDATE' and 'FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE'. Whether sqlglot's _parse_locks sets Lock(update=...) truthy only for FOR UPDATE depends on sqlglot's source. The item has no dependency_sources, and sqlglot is not vendored in the head view. I did not read sqlglot/parser.py. I did not run sqlglot to parse the three forms under MySQL.

Read assert_select_only (readonly.py:583-649). For a plain locking SELECT (single statement, no TABLE token, no INTO, no denied function; e.g. SELECT * FROM t FOR UPDATE): _parse_statements (537-552) only raises on empty SQL, bad dialect, MySQL ambiguity (backslash-escaped quotes, /*! comments, nested comments, ambiguous --) or parse/token errors, none of which a plain lock clause triggers; uses_table_shorthand (79-) only fires on a TABLE keyword token; len(statements)==1 passes; root type Select/Union/Intersect/Except/With is in _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES (336-342) so no root-type refusal; Show branch not taken. In the walk (629-649) the checks run in order: _DML_DDL_TYPES (373-381) does not include exp.Lock; the INTO check needs args['into']; then isinstance(sub, exp.Lock) at 643 raises 'locking reads are not allowed'. The denied-function check comes after and a Lock node is not a Func. So no earlier step refuses or accepts with a different message. Absolute-style input traced: lock hung on a Union root (comment 639-642) is covered since every node is checked and Union is an allowed root. Caveat: a locking SELECT that also has TABLE/INTO/denied function is not 'plain' and gets its own earlier message, which is outside the claim.

readonly.py:643-645 raises a plain UnsafeSqlError('locking reads are not allowed (found FOR UPDATE | FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE)'). ReadOnlyGuardRunner.run_sql (safety/__init__.py:125-129) catches UnsafeSqlError and re-raises UnsafeSqlError('refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: <msg>') from e. So it is not RlsError or WholeRowSelectError. In redacted_refusal_text (rule_sets.py:410-435) the message matches none of the _PARSE_REFUSAL_MARKERS (396-407), _logged_by_guard (438-447) returns False because the cause is an UnsafeSqlError, the message lacks 'side-effecting / DoS / RCE', so line 433-434 returns REDACTED_LOCKING_READ.

ReadOnlyGuardRunner (src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:110-148) has async run_sql(args, context, *, require_base_tables=False) and calls inner.run_sql(args, context) when require_base_tables is False (line 147-148). The _Inner stub in tests/unit/test_safety.py:720-725 (and 572-577) defines async run_sql(self, args, context), matching that call; in the test it is not even reached because the guard refuses first (inner.called is False asserted). RunSqlToolArgs, ToolContext, pd, pytest are imported at test_safety.py:11-16; RunSqlToolArgs(sql=...) and ToolContext.model_construct() are used throughout the file. pyproject.toml:110 sets asyncio_mode = "auto", and pytest-asyncio is a dev dep (line 61), so the bare async test methods run. Not executed; verified by reading.

tests/unit/test_safety.py:423-425 unpacks `sql, dialect, *reason = entry` and calls pytest.raises(UnsafeSqlError, match=reason[0] if reason else None), so the third element is a regex searched against the exception message. Entries at lines 259-262 use 'locking reads'; src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:645 raises UnsafeSqlError(f"locking reads are not allowed (found {found})"), which contains that substring.

The guard side is verified: src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:629-645 walks every node of the single parsed statement (stmt.walk()) and raises UnsafeSqlError on any exp.Lock, so a lock nested in a subquery, a set-operation operand or a CTE is refused once sqlglot produces an exp.Lock node. Whether the claim holds for all the listed forms (FOR UPDATE WAIT 5, lock in a scalar subquery in the SELECT list, lock in an INTERSECT/EXCEPT operand, lock after an accepted SHOW) depends on how sqlglot's MySQL parser handles them: whether it emits exp.Lock, raises a parse error (which still fails closed), or silently drops the clause. The review supplied no dependency_sources and sqlglot source is not in the views, so I could not read the parser from an authorized location, and I did not run any command. Missing evidence: sqlglot's MySQL parser lock handling (_parse_locks) for those four inputs, or a run of assert_select_only on them.

The only lock check is `isinstance(sub, exp.Lock)` at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:643 inside assert_select_only (def at 583). assert_select_only is called only from ReadOnlyGuardRunner (safety/__init__.py:125). factory.py:120-121 wraps with ReadOnlyGuardRunner only if cfg.database.read_only. With read_only=false, the remaining guards are RlsGuardRunner (127-128), RuleSetGuardRunner (131-132) and WholeRowSelectGuardRunner (136-137). Rule-sets call only assert_no_denied_functions (rule_sets.py:352), the function-denylist part, with no Lock check. rule_sets.py:385 and :433 only map the refusal message text. safety/__init__.py:236 also calls only assert_no_denied_functions. grep for exp.Lock finds one hit (readonly.py:643). So 'SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE' with read_only=false plus RLS, a rule-set or refuse_whole_row_selects reaches the connector with no lock refusal, as the doc says. Hostile input traced: that statement through build_agent with read_only=false and all guards configured.

factory.py:139-140 wraps RefusalRedactingRunner only when rule_sets is not None, outside the guards (incl. ReadOnlyGuardRunner at :121). readonly.py:643-645 raises UnsafeSqlError('locking reads are not allowed (found ...)'); rule_sets.py:472-477 catches UnsafeSqlError and re-raises with redacted_refusal_text(exc); rule_sets.py:433-434 maps messages containing 'locking reads are not allowed' to REDACTED_LOCKING_READ (:384-387) = 'refusing to execute SQL: locking reads (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, LOCK IN SHARE MODE) are not allowed', matching the doc text exactly. Earlier branches (parse markers, _logged_by_guard with no cause, whole-row, function) do not intercept this message.

MySQL runner session setup (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:126-154) sets only sql_mode removal, SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY, and MAX_EXECUTION_TIME. No lock_wait_timeout, innodb_lock_wait_timeout, or other lock-related setting is applied. MAX_EXECUTION_TIME bounds SELECT run time, not lock lifetime after the read. Hostile input considered: SELECT ... FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE reaching the runner; nothing in the runner (lines 156-175) blocks it. Read-only session blocks FOR UPDATE but, per the doc's own tested claim, not shared locks. The guard's locking-read rule (doc line 11 and line 282 'rule 8') is the only other layer, so the claim that only rule 8 keeps them out holds for the runner/session layer. The doc line 93 is consistent with the code.

read-only-safety.md lines 36-47 number the deny-walk rules: 5 DML/DDL nested, 6 SELECT INTO, 7 denied functions, 8 locking reads. In readonly.py assert_select_only, an exp.Show root that passes the subkind allowlist (607-619) does not return; it falls to the single `for sub in stmt.walk()` loop (629-649), which enforces DML/DDL types (630-632, rule 5), Select INTO (637-638, rule 6), exp.Lock (643-645, rule 8) and _refuse_denied_function (649, rule 7). So an accepted SHOW passes all of rules 5-8; e.g. SHOW COLUMNS ... WHERE x = sleep(1) reaches the function check.

factory.py:120-121 build_agent wraps the runner in ReadOnlyGuardRunner whenever cfg.database.read_only is true (default). Both query_database (tools/_agent.py:66 -> build_agent) and verify-memory (eval/runner.py:140 -> build_agent) go through build_agent. ReadOnlyGuardRunner.run_sql (safety/__init__.py:121-148) calls assert_select_only before delegating to the inner runner, so refusal happens before execution. assert_select_only (safety/readonly.py:629-645) walks every node of the statement tree and raises UnsafeSqlError on any exp.Lock node (FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE, regardless of NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED/OF options, which are args of the Lock node), including nested in subqueries/CTEs/unions. Tests at tests/unit/test_safety.py:652-654 cover FOR UPDATE NOWAIT and SKIP LOCKED. Absolute-claim trace: a nested subquery or union with a lock is covered by the full-tree walk. Parser-error paths fail closed (safety/__init__.py:130-146). Counter-input: an embedder calling build_sql_runner directly bypasses the guard, but that is not the query_database/verify-memory path the changelog describes.

Trigger split (code conditions in run_sql try/except and assert_select_only pre-lock gates): parse/token error -> outside the trigger (valid SQL parses; and it would still raise UnsafeSqlError); TABLE shorthand -> outside the trigger (input has no TABLE token); statement count != 1 -> outside the trigger (single statement); non-allowed root type -> outside the trigger (Select); DML/DDL or INTO nodes -> outside the trigger (none present); generic Exception branch -> fault alternative that fails closed by raising UnsafeSqlError without calling inner.
